{{Separation axioms}}

In [[mathematics]], a '''weak Hausdorff space''' or '''weakly Hausdorff space''' is a [[topological space]] where the image of every [[Continuous function (topology)|continuous map]] from a [[Compact space|compact]] [[Hausdorff space]] into the space is [[closed set|closed]].<ref>{{citation|last=Hoffmann|first=Rudolf-E.|journal=Archiv der Mathematik|title=On weak Hausdorff spaces|volume=32|issue=5|year=1979|mr=547371|doi=10.1007/BF01238530|pages=487–504}}.</ref> The notion was introduced by M. C. McCord<ref>{{citation|last=McCord|first=M. C.|journal=Transactions of the American Mathematical Society|title=Classifying spaces and infinite symmetric products|volume=146|year=1969|pages=273–298|mr=0251719|doi=10.2307/1995173|doi-access=free|jstor=1995173}}.</ref> to remedy an inconvenience of working with the [[Category (mathematics)|category]] of Hausdorff spaces. It is often used in tandem with [[compactly generated space]]s in [[algebraic topology]]. For that, see the [[category of compactly generated weak Hausdorff spaces]].

Their strictness as [[separation axiom|separation properties]] in increasing order is<ref>J.P. May, ''[http://www.math.uchicago.edu/~may/CONCISE/ConciseRevised.pdf A Concise Course in Algebraic Topology]''. (1999) University of Chicago Press {{isbn|0-226-51183-9}} ''(See chapter 5)''</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Strickland|first=Neil P.|title=The category of CGWH spaces|year=2009|url=http://neil-strickland.staff.shef.ac.uk/courses/homotopy/cgwh.pdf}}</ref>
* [[T1 space|T<sub>1</sub>]]: every single-point set is closed.
* {{nobr|Δ-Hausdorff}}: the image of every [[Path (topology)|path]] is closed.
* {{nobr|weak Hausdorff}}: the image under a continuous map of a compact Hausdorff space is closed.
* {{nobr|KC space}}: every compact subset is closed.
* {{nobr|''k''-Hausdorff}}: every compact subspace is Hausdorff.
* {{nobr|[[Hausdorff space|Hausdorff (T<sub>2</sub>)]]}}: distinct points have disjoint neighborhoods.
These are further described in the below.

==k-Hausdorff spaces==

A '''{{visible anchor|k-Hausdorff space}}'''<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Lawson|first1=J|last2=Madison|first2=B|date=1974|title=Quotients of k-semigroups|journal=Semigroup Forum|volume=9|pages=1–18|doi=10.1007/BF02194829|url=https://eudml.org/doc/134055}}</ref> is a topological space which satisfies any of the following equivalent conditions: 

# Each compact subspace is [[Hausdorff space|Hausdorff]].
# The diagonal <math>\{(x, x) : x \in X\}</math> is [[k-closed set|k-closed]] in <math>X \times X.</math>
#* A subset <math>A \subseteq Y</math> is '''{{visible anchor|k-closed}}''', if <math>A \cap K</math> is closed in <math>K</math> for each compact <math>K \subseteq Y.</math>
# Each compact subspace is closed and strongly locally compact.
#* A space is '''{{visible anchor|strongly locally compact}}''' if for each <math>x \in X</math> and each (not necessarily open) [[Neighborhood (topology)|neighborhood]] <math>U \subseteq X</math> of <math>x,</math> there exists a compact neighborhood <math>V \subseteq X</math> of <math>x</math> such that <math>V \subseteq U.</math>

===Properties===

* A Hausdorff space is k-Hausdorff. For a space is Hausdorff if and only if the diagonal <math>\{(x, x) : x \in X\}</math> is closed in <math>X \times X,</math> and each closed subset is a [[k-closed set]].
* A k-Hausdorff space is KC. A '''{{visible anchor|KC space|KC}}''' is a topological space in which every compact subspace is closed.
* A KC space is weak Hausdorff. For if <math>X</math> is KC and <math>f : K \to X</math> is a continuous map from a compact space <math>K,</math> then <math>f(K)</math> is compact, hence closed.
* To show that the [[Compactly generated space|coherent topology induced by compact Hausdorff subspaces]] preserves the compact Hausdorff subspaces and their subspace topology requires that the space be k-Hausdorff; weak Hausdorff is not enough. Hence k-Hausdorff can be seen as the more fundamental definition.

==Δ-Hausdorff spaces==

A '''{{visible anchor|Δ-Hausdorff space|Δ-Hausdorff}}''' is a topological space where the image of every [[Path (topology)|path]] is closed; that is, if whenever <math>f : [0, 1] \to X</math> is continuous then <math>f([0, 1])</math> is closed in <math>X.</math> Every weak Hausdorff space is <math>\Delta</math>-Hausdorff, and every <math>\Delta</math>-Hausdorff space is a [[T1 space|T<sub>1</sub> space]]. A space is '''{{visible anchor|Δ-generated|Δ-generated space}}''' if its topology is the [[Final topology|finest topology]] such that each map <math>f : \Delta^n \to X</math> from a topological <math>n</math>-simplex <math>\Delta^n</math> to <math>X</math> is continuous. <math>\Delta</math>-Hausdorff spaces are to <math>\Delta</math>-generated spaces as weak Hausdorff spaces are to compactly generated spaces.
